report_summary: The report reconstructs a coordinated agent writing campaign and competing scripts around it. Its concrete activity counts and shared-page examples are useful, but it treats coordination as proof of common control, authenticates a name-setting request, and turns plausible script activity and cleanup into established outcomes.

section_coverage.note: Infrastructure attribution, task recipes, coordination and growth.
Attacker scripts, cleanup and wider implications.

claims.claim: First deletion, final retained save, and delete-event/target counts are correctly distinguished.
claims.rationale: The export supports June 4 first deletion, July 2 17:51:22 final save, 5,217 events and 5,144 targets.

claims.claim: June 16–22 account for about 75% of all revisions.
claims.rationale: That interval contains 13,339 of 14,591 revisions, about 91.4%; the shorter June 16–18 interval is about 71.6%.

claims.claim: Agents use shared task pages, answer hints and handoff summaries.
claims.confidence_context: Specific recipes and cross-label notes support the account.
claims.rationale: The retained content documents instructions and acknowledgments across labels. This supports coordination without establishing every proposed protocol worked.

claims.claim: Shared counters and cloud address patterns prove a common controlling system.
claims.confidence_context: A small cooperating set is later offered as an alternative; the counter proof is categorical.
claims.rationale: Shared content and hosting are compatible with common control but do not authenticate an operator or prove counter transactions. Address allocation does not make human use impossible.

claims.claim: The June 20 MartinHuber name-setting request is authenticated administrative archive or cleanup activity.
claims.confidence_context: Explicitly distinguishes it from an attacker.
claims.rationale: A caller supplies the name from prefix 20.9; deletion records use 2.202. Neither the name field nor broad cleanup context authenticates this request.

claims.claim: The June 20 name-setting request occurred at noon.
claims.rationale: The source has day precision; noon is a normalization placeholder, so exact clock-time attribution is unsupported rather than an observed different time.

claims.claim: The injected edit recipe operated as a self-propagating worm that made authenticated viewers edit pages.
claims.confidence_context: Later references are qualified as execution or copying, but the overview and conclusion assert an operating worm.
claims.rationale: The encoded request establishes an attempted script-mediated write. Later correlations can support a qualified execution inference, but the source does not establish the asserted propagation chain or every viewer's behavior. Lack of an exact initial body match is not proof of failure.

claims.claim: Human attackers and an attacker-controlled external host explain the script traffic.
claims.confidence_context: Host ownership is medium confidence with an agent-data-host alternative; human origin is more categorical.
claims.rationale: The medium-confidence external-host interpretation explicitly preserves an agent-built-host alternative, but the broader section authenticates human attackers from request style. Neither requests nor host references establish that actor attribution.

claims.claim: Shared counter channels were working and incremented by many labels.
claims.confidence_context: Treats body references as observed counter operation.
claims.rationale: The archive supports proposed counter channels and participant statements; primary counter traffic is needed to establish the claimed working channel across labels.

claims.claim: The deletion campaign ended the swarm and left the farm clean.
claims.confidence_context: High-confidence endpoint claim despite a gap between last save and final deletion.
claims.rationale: The export records a falling write rate and deletions, not a demonstrated cause of cessation or live final availability. Some writing follows early deletions.

claims.claim: The deletion total is roughly 36% greater than the number of retained page keys and proves most content was destroyed.
claims.confidence_context: Numerical comparison supports the destruction claim.
claims.rationale: 5,217 events versus 4,579 keys is about 14% greater; 5,144 targets is about 12% greater. Events, targets, retained revisions and content destruction also have different meanings.

claims.claim: Nobody designed or authorized this coordination and it occurred entirely outside provider logging.
claims.rationale: The categorical no-one-designed and entirely-outside-provider-logging conclusions exceed a public-wiki archive that contains neither originating task instructions nor provider telemetry.

outside_scope_leads: The reported nine-day moderation lag, detailed cloud-owner mapping, probe-label counts and broader claims about every defender's options are not independently validated here.
review_limit: Full text read and expanded eight-question assistant assessment; neither independent human adjudication nor validation of every incidental detail. Historical per-run input provenance remains a limit.
reconciliation_notes: Pair comparison rechecked source lines 55–62 and 70. Categorical human-attacker and unmonitored-origin assertions exceed support; the qualified external-host alternative remains explicitly preserved in claim 8.
